newsitem.title: UK: UK January 1997 retail sales to jump 10% y/y-CEBR.
newsitem.headline: UK January 1997 retail sales to jump 10% y/y-CEBR.

text.p: British retail sales are likely to leap in January, to more than 10 percent above the same month a year ago, the Centre for Economics and Business Research said on Friday.
Mark Pragnell, senior economist at the Centre, forecasts UK non-food stores will record sales worth 6.4 billion stg in January 1997, up 10.3 percent from January 1996.
Britain's high street retailers traditionally cut prices after the Christmas period -- the so-called January sales.

"The year-on-year increase is likely to be the fastest since 1988," Pragnell said. "Rising incomes, year-end bonuses and reduced rates of redundancy mean people have both the means and the confidence to spend."
"The last time this happened was in the late 1980s."

But given that the late-80s boom followed on from four solid years of sales growth, while next year's sales will follow six years of bad or average January sales, the CEBR said it would take another good year to recreate the spirit of the 1980s.
It also forecast that price discounts will be smaller than in the previous two years.
